Guide & Academy/BA Lending Academy/Module 7

Module 7 of 11

LWS — Workflow and human control

The system that moves people: queues, approvals, complaints and cases — with every action attributed.

Between the automated planes sits the Loan Workflow System: derived task queues with SLA clocks, the maker-checker fabric that satisfies segregation-of-duties law, and the two workflows regulators read first — grievance redressal and fraud case handling.

Lesson 7.1 · 15 min

Task queues, SLA clocks and attribution

  • Explain derived queues — tasks computed from domain state, not created by hand
  • Describe SLA clocks, priorities and breach handling
  • State why every action carries actor attribution

Lesson 7.2 · 16 min

Maker-checker, exceptions and committees

  • Explain segregation of duties as implemented, not aspirational
  • Describe approval matrices and exception taxonomies
  • Understand committee workflows and their evidence packs

Lesson 7.3 · 18 min

Grievance redressal and fraud case workflow

  • Walk the complaint lifecycle and its 30-day statutory clock
  • Explain RBI CMS/Ombudsman escalation
  • Contrast grievance handling with the fraud case's natural-justice track
